heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles NinjaTek NinjaFlex 85A out of the box using its tight-tolerance direct drive extruder, but prints must be capped at 33 mm/s corresponding to a 2.8 mm³/s max volumetric speed. No hardened nozzle or heated enclosure is required, though bypassing the AMS in favor of the external spool holder is mandatory to prevent feeding jams.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + Glue Stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap 'Max volumetric speed' at exactly 2.8 mm³/s in the filament settings to automatically throttle all feature speeds below the 33 mm/s limit.
Disable 'Reduce infill retraction' and enable 'Avoid crossing walls' (Max detour length: 0) to minimize oozing and travel moves across printed boundaries.
Lower internal and external solid infill speeds manually to 30 mm/s to eliminate backpressure spikes in the melt zone.
Set Pressure Advance / Flow Dynamics factor to roughly 0.12 - 0.18 via manual calibration to compensate for high elastomeric flex.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Filament wrapping around drive gears (extruding out the side)
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Backpressure generated by printing faster than the 2.8 mm³/s volumetric limit or printing too cold.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Ensure print speed does not exceed 33 mm/s, raise nozzle temp to 235°C, and bypass the AMS directly to the external spool.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and surface bubbling across perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High moisture absorption in the 85A polyurethane matrix causing steam flash boiling in the hotend.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated convection dryer at 65°C for at least 8 hours prior to printing and print from a dry box.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Permanent bed adhesion or torn PEI coating upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Direct chemical bonding between molten TPU and bare PEI surface without a sacrificial barrier.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a generous, uniform layer of PVA glue stick or liquid adhesive as a separation agent before starting the print.

faq.question: Can I feed NinjaTek NinjaFlex 85A through the Bambu Lab AMS Lite?
faq.answer: No. The 85A shore hardness is far too elastic and flexible for the AMS Lite drive mechanics and PTFE tubing. You must feed it from the external spool holder directly into the toolhead.

faq.question: Do I need to install a hardened steel nozzle to print NinjaFlex on the A1?
faq.answer: No. NinjaFlex 85A is an unfilled, non-abrasive thermoplastic polyurethane, making the stock stainless steel nozzle fully compatible without excessive wear.

faq.question: Why is the print speed capped so low at 33 mm/s?
faq.answer: Due to high elasticity, soft 85A TPU buckles easily in the direct drive throat when backpressure exceeds 2.8 mm³/s volumetric flow, which limits standard 0.2mm layer height printing to 33 mm/s.

faq.question: How should I remove the printed TPU part from the Textured PEI plate safely?
faq.answer: Allow the bed to completely cool to room temperature, then gently flex the plate. If it still adheres tightly, apply isopropyl alcohol around the edges to dissolve the glue stick release barrier.
